item.text: I’m reviewing the current builder-based design to find the next structural cleanup. The likely target is consolidating duplicated vertex validation and tightening the graph API around reusable base behavior.

I found the next worthwhile refactor: make the builder conform to the same `Graph` contract as the finished graph. That removes duplicated vertex validation and keeps the code centered on one abstraction instead of separate ad hoc APIs.

The builder now participates in the same graph abstraction as the immutable graph. I’m compiling and running again, then I’ll inspect the updated builder to confirm the validation duplication is actually gone.

I continued the refactor by making [graph/GraphBuilder.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/graph/GraphBuilder.java:7) implement `Graph` directly. That means the builder now exposes `vertexCount()` and `neighborsOf(...)` like the finished graph, and it reuses `Graph.requireVertex(...)` instead of carrying its own separate validation helper. The result is a cleaner API surface centered on one graph contract rather than parallel mutable and immutable shapes.

Internally, the builder now keeps stable read-only neighbor views during construction, so partial graphs can be inspected through the same interface as completed ones.
